_comment: The Russian Federation's construction base — a Soviet-industrial pile with a dome.
Authored from the four-view turnaround at incoming/factions/russian-federation/
structures/base/ (gitignored: third-party rights, and it informs PARAMETERS only).
A front/rear/left/right sheet is the ideal modelling reference, because massing and
proportion can be read straight off it instead of guessed from one oblique photograph.
Scale from measured peers, not taste: the GLA barracks is 110 x 51 x 88 world units at
565 triangles, the war factory 100 x 58 x 122 at 684.
WHAT THE BUDGET BUYS IS THE SILHOUETTE, NOT THE PIPEWORK. The reference is dense with
gantry cranes, rail spurs, pipe runs and crates — all of it scene dressing around the
building rather than the building. At ~650 triangles the things that must read are the
dome, the drum it sits on, the entrance portico and the stacks. Everything else is a
+X is FORWARD: the entrance faces +X, so the portico projects that way and the stacks
sit at the rear. Z is up and z = 0 is the ground, so `at` is the CENTRE of a part.
The drum is 12-sided ON PURPOSE. The reference has vertical ribs around it, and a radial
array is not something this recipe format has — but a 12-gon already reads as ribbed at
RTS camera distance, and it costs 44 triangles instead of a rib array's several hundred.
name: RFBASE
_texture: Three materials. Cold grey concrete for the mass, a darker ribbed metal for the dome,
THE STACK BANDS ARE THE INTERESTING ONE. A band lives in texture V, and under cube
projection V maps to world Z on any vertical surface — so on a standing cylinder a
texture band IS a horizontal band at a real height, which is exactly the red-and-white
banding the reference has. The same feature was WRONG on the Mangal, where it crossed the
hull, the tracks and the gun barrel at one height. The lesson is not that bands are bad,
it is that cube projection makes texture V mean world height, so a band belongs only on
parts that are meant to be banded.
Everything TILES: measured, 61.9% of the 3,790 retail meshes with texcoords have UVs
outside 0..1, so the engine wraps and these are MATERIALS, not unwrapped atlases.

rfbase.tga._: Poured concrete. Large panels, low wear, almost no rivets — it is cast, not welded.

rfbase_dome.tga._: Ribbed sheet metal, darker and cooler than the concrete so the dome separates from
rfbase_dome.tga.__: the drum it stands on. Narrow panels read as ribs at this distance.
rfbase_dome.tga._lighten: Three darkening passes stack on a dome: the material's own occlusion, the rib painter's valleys, and a Cycles bake of a surface curving away from every light. Authored at the flanks' tone it renders as a black cap.

rfbase_stack.tga._: Banded stacks: two red bands on dirty white. See the note above about why this works
rfbase_stack.tga.__: here and not on a tank.

rfbase_ribbed.tga._: Concrete with pilasters — the wings and the drum. Same base as the mass so the building stays one material, with structure cut into it rather than colour.

rfbase_pipes.tga._: The machine hall's pipe runs and conduit banks, with a flange every few units.

rfbase_sign.tga._: The entrance sign band. Deep red with a white rule, which is what the reference has under its lettering — the lettering itself is beyond what a 256px region can hold at this scale and is deliberately not attempted.

rfbase_win.tga._: Concrete with rows of windows: dark glass, a lit sill under it, a shadowed reveal above. A few panes lit, deterministically — a perfectly uniform grid reads as a texture, an irregular one as a building with people in it.

rfbase_door.tga._: The dark interior behind the entrance arch.

parts._: Battered podium. taper < 1 leans the walls inward, which is what reads as poured
parts.__: concrete mass rather than a box sitting on grass.
parts.name: PODIUM

parts._: The drum the dome sits on. See the note above about 12 sides standing in for ribs.
parts.name: DRUM
parts._paint: Ribbed, and it replaces geometry: the 12-gon already stands in for the reference's vertical ribs at silhouette level, and the painter puts the rest of them on the surface for nothing. The reference's drum is a colonnade — many more uprights than a 12-gon has corners.

parts._: THE DOME. The whole reason `dome` exists as a shape. 3 rings is enough at this
parts.__: size — the silhouette is a half-circle and extra rings buy interior shading
parts.___: nobody sees. Its base sits exactly on the drum's top at z = 32.
parts.name: DOME

parts._: Entrance portico, projecting forward, with the archway cut clean through its front
parts.__: face. NOTE the cut is in the PART's local frame — the part is still at the origin
parts.___: when a boolean runs, so this is x +6 of the portico's own centre, not of the
parts.____: world's. A doorway is the one thing a texture genuinely cannot fake, because the
parts._____: silhouette has to have a hole in it.
parts.name: PORTICO

_: The back of the archway. Without it the cut looks straight through the building and
the entrance reads as damage. Set back 5 units so the reveal has depth, and dark, so
it reads as an interior rather than as another wall.
parts.name: DOORWAY

parts._: The sign band over the entrance — СОВЕТСКАЯ КОНСТРУКЦИОННАЯ БАЗА in the
parts.__: reference. Geometry, not just painted on, because the reference's band stands
parts.___: proud of the wall and catches its own shadow line. The lettering is the
parts.name: SIGNBAND

parts._: Flanking halls, one authored and mirrored across Y. Taller than the podium and
parts.__: lower than the dome, which is what keeps the dome reading as the centrepiece.
parts.name: WINGS
parts._paint: Pilasters. Fewer and heavier than the drum's ribs, so they read as buttresses.

parts._: Rear machine hall — the block the stacks stand on.
parts.name: REARBLOCK

parts._: Stacks, mirrored across Y. Deliberately TALLER than the dome: in the reference
parts.__: they are the highest thing on the site, and a stack that stops below the dome
parts.___: reads as a vent. The red and white banding is texture.
parts.name: STACKS
